questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- that I could follow relevant courses (in regards to my field of study as well as personal interests)
- that the courses were taught in English
- the destination/city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been an unforgettable and important experience - both in terms of personal and academic growth

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The receiving institution gave good and clear instructions. Easy to ask for help if needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A well organized introduction day with general instructions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult to find because I was out late - so starting in good time is recommended. The host institution helped to find a good accommodation with short notice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find a place that is easy to commute to

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was easy. The administrative part was clear to follow. Only problem was delay in getting certain papers signed but it was easy to get in touch with the host institution with any kind of problems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Available contact person (help via mail)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To limit delays as much as possible - make sure your papers are in order from the beginning!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was high

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied from class to class. Each professor had a very unique style of teaching - more or less similar to those of UCPH. The level of teaching was high (as at UCPH) but the readings for the classes where (in general) less demanding. Since I followed 6 different courses at my host institution the professors had varying (personal) professional careers outside of the university - which was very inspiring but It also ment that they had very different expectations for the students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Great Books
- Investigative Journalism
- Portuguese Contemporary History 
- Cultural and Creative Industries
- International Relations
- Culture and Globalization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Relations: educating, well taught, super interesting and relevant course!
Portuguese Contemporary History: I would definitely recommend taking a history course to get knowledge about the host country

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Socializing with the people you live with! Going on museum trips! Exploring the city!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going for random walks in the different neighborhoods of the city. Using the opportunity to see more of the country (the Azores are a must!!!!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - people where welcoming and nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To go live in a housing that doesn't only have international students (usually the accommodation found through your host university will be accommodating more local people). Talking with local students in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Every part. The language! The people! The country! The Azores!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: notice that you will be most likely following multiple courses of different levels/ with different professors/ in different fields - this can lead to some confusion at the beginning. 

2: your fellow students are your friends!! if you feel like you have academic and/or personal problems they probably have them too - help each other out!

3: use the help available - both from the administration and the professors. They are generally glad to help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They check level of attendance meaning that you cannot miss more than 9 classes pr. course - this might be stresfull at the beginning but is totally manageable.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences of living in a country rich in culture and history - and getting to know it besides people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying focused on University work

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would recommend going on an exchange to EVERYONE. It is a roller-coaster worth every high and low.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
